lxml XMLParser is created with resolve_entities=True, load_dtd=True, and no_network=False. Combined with etree.fromstring() on attacker-controlled request.body, this allows XXE (XML External Entity) attacks to read arbitrary files on the server (e.g., /etc/passwd), perform SSRF, or cause DoS via entity expansion (billion laughs).

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: request.GET.get('blob') data is encoded as UTF-8 and decoded with base64 before being passed to pickle.loads(). While the base64-encoded data is user-controlled, this provides an obfuscation layer. When combined with the file-write endpoint, an attacker can upload a crafted pickle payload that gets decoded and deserialized, enabling RCE.

The Origin header from request.headers is taken directly from the HTTP request and reflected into CORS response headers (Access-Control-Allow-Origin and Access-Control-Allow-Credentials). An attacker can set a malicious Origin header to bypass CORS protections, allowing arbitrary origins to make credential-based cross-origin requests against this API.
The response explicitly sets X-XSS-Protection to '0' and Content-Security-Policy to an empty string, disabling browser-side XSS and content-type sniffing protections for this endpoint.

The full request body and the Authorization bearer token are logged via logger.warning. While logged with WARNING level, this means sensitive credentials (authorization tokens) and potentially confidential request payloads are written to the application log, leading to information disclosure.

extra.message: The SECRET_KEY falls back to the hardcoded string 'insecure-local-dev-key-change-me' when DJANGO_SECRET_KEY environment variable is not set. In production or any non-development deployment, this exposes session tokens and cryptographic material to all who read the source code.

All /ops/* endpoints share a single authentication mechanism (_wrk_gate) that relies on a single environment variable (INTERNAL_OPS_TOKEN) compared against a single header (x-internal-token). This is the only access control and provides no authorization, audit logging, IP whitelisting, or per-endpoint permissions. Any service knowing this token can interact with all 15 operations endpoints, including code-injection, XSS, unserialization, path traversal, and NoSQL injection sinks.

The deadline_complete view at line 676-684 (and task_status_update at 626-637) are missing @require_POST decorator, allowing CSRF attacks where GET requests can be used to mark deadlines/tasks as completed without a CSRF token. While middleware provides baseline CSRF protection via @login_required, the absence of @require_POST on mutation endpoints is a deviation from defense-in-depth.

The case_client_packet_078 endpoint returns the hardcoded value 'tok_live_partner_sync' as the 'sync_key' response field. This appears to be a credential or secret token that is exposed to any caller who passes the internal token check. The 'tax_ref' value '739-44-1982' also appears to be hardcoded PII.
